title: No structural-survey/shape-count analysis reduction: skeleton surveys and arch ratchets run on rg + targeted reads
wanted_capability: An analysis reduction (for example analysis.matchShape or analysis.structuralSurvey) that answers a structural predicate across a repo-bounded file set with a count, the matching file list, and a capped set of exemplar spans, computed host-side so the isolate never receives the full capture fan-out. Predicates cover shapes such as extends/implements, annotated-with, a type injecting another type, and field-injection sites. The same tool serves skeleton surveys and baseline-and-ratchet violation counts.
missing_primitive: analysis.matchShape / analysis.structuralSurvey: repo-bounded count + file list + capped exemplars for a structural predicate
fallback_used: Skeleton surveys run rg/grep/find + targeted file reads per detection signature; arch-ratchet calibration counts violations with an ad-hoc ArchUnit rule. analysis.references covers symbol-name reference counts only, not structural shapes; code.query is per-file tree-sitter, aggregate-capped, and returns heap-heavy spans.
evidence: crates/bro-harness/src/bindings/code_facts.rs: CodeQuery (per-file tree-sitter captures, capped at MAX_AGGREGATE_QUERY_CAPTURES, returns full spans)
notes: Tier 1 per the toolbox gap map (§5). Fits the facts-vs-analysis two-tier philosophy exactly: a structural question answered as a Rust-side reduction. Entry activity for the entire campaign portfolio (dozens of concerns), so leverage is breadth, not depth on one concern.
resolution_note: Transferred to https://github.com/daystrom-institute/blackbox/issues/21, now the canonical implementation work item. Structural predicate counts with bounded exemplars remain unimplemented; existing reference counts and per-file query captures do not supply the requested reduction. Verified against accepted beta 93c2d391a8d6b8d2d760b88b1acdadbafc7a3ea4. Gap triage is complete; the GitHub issue remains open and this transfer does not claim the capability is implemented.
